clue.text: A cat confronting a bird intended to make a kill

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a hawk is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A cat squares up to a bird of prey, each bent on a kill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confronting' only sets the cat beside the bird. The definition describes a weapon, a hatchet made for striking.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American war axe is a weapon, made for striking and killing.

clue.text: Royalty changing direction could be routed

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters may be rearranged into another word
E and S are compass points, so swapping east for south in the word routed is a change of direction

explanation.surface: A royal party taking a new route could be put to flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing direction' turns the E (east) of ROUTED into S (south), giving ROUTSD; 'could be' then rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Tudor was the English royal dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Book a young woman driver without much experience

parts.note: miss is a title or term for a young unmarried woman
L is the learner driver, from the L-plate displayed in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone books a young woman as a novice driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb but is the definition, a noun. In Britain a learner driver shows an L-plate, so L means learner.
explanation.definitionFit: A missal is the service book holding the texts of the Catholic Mass.

clue.text: Sound animal, though croaky

indicators.note: sound tells the solver to say the word for the animal out loud and write down the like-sounding word

parts.note: a horse is an animal

explanation.surface: An animal is healthy even though it croaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' reads as 'healthy', describing the animal, but it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough, husky voice, as from a sore throat, is croaky.

clue.text: One may get intoxicated on non-alcoholic drink — here's proof!

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits below it, so this word comes after the drink

parts.note: water is a drink with no alcohol in it
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Drink water and still get drunk? There's the evidence!
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes about getting drunk on water. 'proof' is used as in 'waterproof': able to keep something out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sealed against leaks is impervious, as in the suffix of 'bulletproof'.

clue.text: When companies raise capital

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
sets are groups or companies of people

explanation.surface: This is the moment when firms go out to raise money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' only joins the wordplay to the definition, reading as 'make up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's capital is the property and money it holds, its resources of value.

clue.text: With money in the bag, promises to pay can be wide-ranging

indicators.note: in puts the money inside the bag

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch
P stands for pence, small British money
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: With cash safely bagged, IOUs can stretch a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money' as P is short for pence, Britain's small coin; 'With' and 'can be' only link the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something roomy covers a large area, so it is broad or wide-ranging.

clue.text: Note taking up with new choir will have blissful result

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: new tells the solver to make something fresh from the letters of the word choir

explanation.surface: A singer's new choir taking up a note produces a joyous sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the five letters of CHOIR; 'will have ... result' is padding linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is intense happiness, so feeling it is being elated or blissful.

clue.text: Stepping out free is admitted by cheat

indicators.note: is admitted by means one word is let inside the other

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick, a cheat
to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: A prisoner walking out at liberty is let in by a swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stepping out' looks like leaving, but it is the definition, walking with long strides; 'is admitted by' signals one word going inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking with long purposeful steps is walking out briskly, stepping out.

clue.text: Abhorrence is stated — devastation

indicators.note: devastation suggests the letters of is stated are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone declares their loathing of the destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devastation' reads as the thing loathed, but it signals rearranging IS STATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is strong dislike, so it shares the sense of loathing.

clue.text: A poor actor gets by with a big basket

parts.note: a ham is an overacting, poor actor
per means by, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: A bad actor makes off with a large basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'with' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a large lidded wicker basket, as for a picnic.

clue.text: Respecting a fool on the river to give encouragement

parts.note: re means concerning or respecting
an ass is a fool
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Someone cheers up a fool who is by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England, a crossword favourite. 'on' and 'to' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone's confidence is to hearten or give encouragement.

clue.text: An English gentleman is bland about gold

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: mild means gentle or bland
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An English gentleman is dull, for all his gold.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for gold comes from heraldry. The word was used on the Continent for a rich travelling Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: Milord was a continental form of address for an English lord or wealthy gentleman.

clue.text: Shifty storemen in the soup

indicators.note: shifty suggests the letters of storemen in are moved about

explanation.surface: Dodgy warehousemen are in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' looks like the idiom for being in trouble, but 'in' is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup with pasta.

clue.text: Obscure union — it might well be weakening

parts.note: dim means obscure or faint

indicators.note: might well be signals that the letters of union and it can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shadowy trade union may be losing its strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might well be' rearranges the letters of UNION and IT together; the dash between them is only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A diminution is a reduction or lessening, a weakening.

clue.text: Practically of equal value

definitions.meaning: equal in worth, as in 'one is ... the other'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'virtually' and 'equally good', as in 'as good as new'.

clue.text: Stands up for proposals

definitions.meaning: juts out or protrudes above the rest

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means sticks out; as a plural noun it means planned undertakings.

clue.text: Make known underworld boss secure

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god who rules the underworld
to close is to shut or secure

explanation.surface: A gangland chief reveals how he locks up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underworld boss' suggests a gangster, but Dis is the Roman god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclose is to reveal or make public.

clue.text: Eliminate all crooks!

parts.note: reads as a call to wipe out criminals, but crooks are bends to be taken out of something bent

explanation.definitionFit: To remove every bend from something is to make it free of curves.

clue.text: Put together and painted

definitions.meaning: assembled or invented, as a story

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both invented or assembled and wearing cosmetics.

clue.text: In a restaurant some serving men show bottle

indicators.note: in places the servicemen inside the eatery

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant
the RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of serving soldiers

explanation.surface: In an eatery, some waiters bring out a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving men' suggests waiters, but they are soldiers: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British Army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is an open-topped glass flask for serving wine or water.

clue.text: A space-traveller is satisfied with seafood when going up

parts.note: met means satisfied, as in 'demands were met'

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word roe is read from the bottom up

parts.note: roe is fish eggs, a seafood

explanation.surface: An astronaut is content with a fish supper on the way up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A space-traveller' suggests an astronaut, but it is a shooting star; 'when going up' turns the seafood word in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteor is a rock from space burning up as it enters the atmosphere.

clue.text: The aim of protest

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means a purpose or goal; as a verb, to oppose.

clue.text: Neat bars can get messed up in Ireland

indicators.note: messed up tells the solver the letters of neat bars are to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Tidy pubs can become a shambles in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'in Ireland', for a place there: Strabane is a town in County Tyrone, Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Strabane is a town in County Tyrone, on the border of Northern Ireland and the Republic.

clue.text: American lawyer given credit over certain material

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
on can mean over, as in a lid on a jar

explanation.surface: A US attorney gets credit for a particular fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a linking word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dacron is a trade name for a polyester fibre, a particular synthetic fabric.

clue.text: Slacken speed after a fashion

indicators.note: after means the speed word follows the fashion word

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Someone slows down, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a fashion' looks like the idiom for 'to some extent', but 'after' here only orders the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate is to make less intense, to ease off or slacken.

clue.text: The nurse in charge of some wards is terribly stern

definitions.text: The nurse in charge of some wards is terribly stern

indicators.note: some tells the solver that only part of the run of words that follows is needed, with letters lying across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A ward's head nurse is fearsomely strict.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'wards is terribly'; read whole, the clue paints the formidable senior nurse running a British hospital ward, the stock figure behind the title.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the senior nurse in charge of a hospital ward is traditionally given this title.

clue.text: Time for the high jump contest?

definitions.text: Time for the high jump contest?

parts.words: Time for the high jump contest?
parts.note: reads as an athletics event, but a jump in time is the extra day added every fourth February

explanation.definitionFit: Every fourth year an extra day, 29 February, is added to the calendar.
